title: Ash-Shams: the soul
hookLine: by the soul and its shaping, successful is the one who purifies it (91:7–10)
carry: the one who purifies it succeeds

cards: And then the last thing Ash-Shams swears by, something small enough to fit inside a person. Not a star, not a mountain. A soul.
Yours, and everyone's. The whole sky was the windup. After all that, the surah says one thing about the soul, one sentence about what success actually is.

teach.b: Verse seven: by the soul, nafs, and the One who shaped it and made it well-proportioned. Verse eight: and inspired it with its wickedness and its mindfulness. Both, in the same soul, from the start.

The surah doesn't pretend people are pure by default, or rotten by default. The soul knows both roads. Then the sentence the oaths were building to, in Pickthall's words: He is indeed successful who causeth it to grow.
And the next verse, the mirror: the one who buries it, who stunts it, has failed. The Arabic verb for the first is zakkaha. You've heard the root: zakat, the giving that is one of the five pillars.

teach.h: ZAKKAHA — TO PURIFY AND TO GROW.
teach.b: Z-k-y carries two ideas at once, to purify and to grow, the way pruning a plant cleans it and makes it grow stronger. Zakat purifies wealth, and this verse says a person can do the same to a soul.

teach.h: DASSAHA — TO BURY IT IN THE DIRT.
teach.b: The opposite verb, dassaha, means to bury something, to hide it in the dirt. Later scholars gave the work of the first verb a name: tazkiyah, purification of the soul. But the verse itself is plain.
Success here isn't money or followers.

teach.h: SUCCESS: WHAT YOU DID WITH IT.
teach.b: It's what you did with the soul you were given: did you tend it, or bury it?

teach.h: THE ONE WHO PURIFIES IT SUCCEEDS.
teach.b: The surah then ends with a short, sharp story: the people of Thamud, who hamstrung the she-camel they'd been warned to leave alone. A soul buried, a whole people at a time.

how: Muslims speak of tazkiyah, the lifelong work of purifying the soul, through prayer, remembrance, charity and watching one's habits; the verse on success in Ash-Shams is often quoted about it.

o: the shade travelers seek in the noon heat
the sun, Surah ninety-one of the Qur'an
the blazing heat on the Day of Judgment

games.q: what's inside the verses — tap the pairs.

s: Ash-Shams says the soul starts out purely good
it says the soul was inspired with both its wickedness and its mindfulness.
the verb for purifying the soul shares a root with zakat
z-k-y: to purify and to grow, like pruning a plant.
the surah defines success as wealth and standing
success is the one who purifies the soul; failure is the one who buries it.

games.q: after its run of oaths, Ash-Shams names who is successful. who is it?
o: the one who is never tempted
the one who purifies the soul
the one who knows the most
games.why: the one who makes it grow and purifies it (91:9). the soul knows both roads; success is what you tend.

practice: Think of one small habit that clouds your day a little: the scroll before sleep, the sharp reply, the thing you say about a coworker. Picture pruning it, one cut, not a whole new life, and see what the cut would look like.
If you pray, you can ask for help with it in your own words.

wordCard.voice: Ash-Shams. The sun, Surah ninety-one, whose oaths end on the soul: successful is the one who purifies it. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: "purified it," from z-k-y, to purify and to grow, the root of zakat (Qur'an 91:9).

carryVoice: Your line: the one who purifies it succeeds. Tending is done in small cuts. One hundred ninety-two days in.

sources.q: He is indeed successful who causeth it to grow

sources.ref: Qur'an 91:7–8, 91:10 (the soul shaped and inspired; the one who stunts it)
